H [13] CN and HC 3 N, showing highest linearity in the L bol -to-L mol (p) scaling relations, may serve as the most effective tracers for the dense molecular gas mass among the six molecular line tracers.

In contrast, HCN and HCO [+] exhibit a significantly sublinear trend in the L bol -to-L mol (p) scaling relations due to the effects of optical thickness, which diminishes their effectiveness as tracers for gravitationally bound gas.

Across three distinct distance intervals — those less than 3 kpc, those ranging from 3 to 6 kpc, and those greater than 6 kpc — there is no discernible trend between the slope s of the power-law tails and the L/M ratio or the density of the clumps.
The ratios of L bol -to-L mol ( ? ), serving as indicators of star formation efficiency within massive star-forming clumps, exhibit a weak anti-correlation with the power-law index in the I-PDF.
In addition, the star formation efficiency is also weakly anti-correlated with the exponent U of the corresponding equivalent density distribution.

Our findings suggest that the scaling relationships between L bol and L mol ( ? ) for HCN and HCO [+] are sublinear, indicating that these molecules might not be the most effective tracers for the dense gas.
In contrast, H [13] CN and HC 3 N exhibit a nearly linear relationship between L bol and L mol ( ? ), indicating that they can well trace gravitationally bound dense gas.
